title: One-Pan Creamy Pesto Chicken and Penne
description: Make creamy pesto chicken pasta in just one pan with zero boiling required. Skip the $35 DoorDash fee and eat in under twenty minutes tonight.
storyHeading: Why This Saved My Tuesday Night
story: Walking through my front door at 6:30 PM with zero groceries and a stubborn refusal to pay thirty-five bucks for lukewarm takeout is my weekly Olympic sport. That panic led me to dump dry penne, chicken breast, and chicken broth into a single skillet one desperate evening. When I first tested this, I made the amateur mistake of dumping store-bought heavy cream in at the very beginning with the simmering broth, which caused it to separate into an oily mess. Lesson learned: the cream and the jarred pesto go in at the very end off the direct heat, letting the residual starch from the pasta naturally thicken everything into a glossy, velvety sauce without curdling. It beats washing two pots any day of the week.
ingredients: 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized chunks
1/3 cup prepared basil pesto (Costco Kirkland brand works great)
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat, add the chicken chunks, season with salt and pepper, and sear until golden brown on most sides, about 5 minutes.

Pour the dry penne pasta and chicken broth directly into the skillet with the chicken, bring everything to a rolling boil, then immediately turn the heat down to medium-low and cover tightly with a lid.
Simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring once or twice halfway through, until the pasta is tender and most of the broth has been absorbed or evaporated.
Remove the skillet from the heat source completely, then stir in the heavy cream, jarred pesto, and shredded parmesan until a smooth, glossy sauce coats the pasta.
proHack: Do not skip removing the pan from the heat before stirring in the cream and pesto. High heat will cause the oil in the pesto to separate and give your sauce a greasy texture instead of a silky finish.
servingIdea: Serve warm with a handful of peppery baby arugula tossed in lemon juice and a warm slice of garlic-buttered French bread.
storage: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat on the stovetop over medium-low heat with a splash of milk or water to bring the creamy sauce back to life.

faqs.question: Can I use chicken thighs instead of breasts?
faqs.answer: Definitely. Boneless skinless chicken thighs actually stay juicier when simmered directly in the skillet liquids.

faqs.question: What if my pasta is still crunchy and the liquid is gone?
faqs.answer: Just splash in another quarter cup of water or chicken broth, put the lid back on, and let it simmer for two more minutes.
